title: St. Louis excursion boats: Creath, Fate Marable and the Wishart Line
summary: Shoffner describes Creath and Marable's rival boats docking at Olive Street, the musicians on them, and the Wishart Line's attempt to cut in.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: That's right, that's right. Yeah. Now you see, Charlie was playing on the same pole and Faith Marable with Lois Armstrong and Baby Dots, Johnny Sincere, Dave Jones, oh this other clarinet player, trumpet player. He was playing the first trumpet player. He was playing saxophone now, he lives in Milwaukee now. Oh, I don't remember. It would come across from the mind.
Yeah, was Pop Foster in the band then too, bass player? Yeah, Pop Foster and Pop Foss was playing bass.
Well they was playing on the GS.

And you were at Charlie Crest was on the St. Paul. They both docked right at the end of Olive Street to St. Louis. You see? Did they both work out from there or one go up the river usually? No, now coming up, Faith brought the GS up to St. Paul, up to St. Paul, I mean St. Paul, up to St. Louis. And then the GS was brought down from the Diodocs up in the Redempo Highway. See? And they both run out of St. Louis during the summer. Yeah. You see?
Two different excursions the same night sometime, would it be that way? That's right. I didn't know.

Two different excursions, but it was two different boats. It was like that. Then the Wishart Line tried to cut in there, Captain Wishart. Now he brought in a line up, come up from New Orleans, it was called the Wishart Line. And his boat was a flat, flat bottom boat. The rest of them was...
Remember the name of any of his boats? No, I don't remember. I don't remember the Washington...
